rv.q: Sad to report, it is a strange and largely unsatisfactory experience.

The ultimate impression is of a weird evening in which two great actors are left struggling to find their characters, and sometimes even their lines, and in which the great and noble cause of age-blind casting suffers a decisive setback.
It’s a reading that goes against the grain, but one that brings a certain friction to a comedy of contradictions.
Rylance says that all the impetus for this production came from Redgrave and Jones’ desire to perform it: it’s a desire that should have been strangled early.
Nevertheless the production is a car crash.

cn.t: Mark Rylance's unconventional casting of elderly stars Vanessa Redgrave and James Earl Jones as Beatrice and Benedick divides critics, with most finding the age-defying choice misguided and the comedy falling flat.
